sections.title: Block catalog

blocks.text: Every block type `build.py` renders appears below once, in a small library's lending process: what it is for, when to use it and when not, the block itself, and the JSON that drew it.

No block needs a profile: all of them render under any profile, and the choice file's features decide which a report may use. Some have a usual home: `media` and `resources` belong to web-research, `gallery` to app-audit, and `argument`, `example` and `compare` to explanation. This page uses explanation.

sections.title: p: a paragraph of prose

blocks.text: Use it for every claim and its reason, and as the lead sentence before any list, table or figure. Avoid it for parallel items a reader scans or compares; those belong in a list or a table.
A member can borrow a book for three weeks, because the loan rules give every title the same period unless it is on reserve.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "p",
  "text": "A member can borrow a book for three weeks, because the loan rules give every title the same period unless it is on reserve."
}

sections.title: bullets: an unordered list

blocks.text: Use it for a few parallel points whose order does not matter. Avoid it for a sequence (take `steps`) or for items that carry several fields (take a `table`).

items: No overdue fines above the limit

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "bullets",
  "items": [
    "A member card",
    "The books on the counter",
    "No overdue fines above the limit"
  ]
}

sections.title: steps: a numbered sequence

blocks.text: Use it for actions a person does in a fixed order. Avoid it for a process with branches or several actors; draw a `flow` instead.

items: Hand over the receipt with the due dates.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "steps",
  "items": [
    "Scan the member card.",
    "Scan each book.",
    "Hand over the receipt with the due dates."
  ]
}

sections.title: callout: a framed answer, warning, action or note

blocks.text: Use it to lift out the one answer, safety warning or next action a reader must not miss. Avoid it for ordinary emphasis; more than one or two callouts per page and none stands out.

blocks.title: Renew before the due date
blocks.text: A loan renews online only while nobody has reserved the book.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "callout",
  "tone": "action",
  "title": "Renew before the due date",
  "text": "A loan renews online only while nobody has reserved the book."
}

sections.title: html: raw HTML as an escape hatch

blocks.text: Use it for small markup no other block offers, such as the JSON listings on this page. Avoid it for anything a block can express, because raw HTML skips the build's checks, links and print rules.

blocks.html: At the self-service kiosk, Esc cancels a loan before the receipt prints.

{
  "type": "html",
  "html": "<p>At the self-service kiosk, <kbd>Esc</kbd> cancels a loan before the receipt prints.</p>"
}

sections.title: argument: a claim with its reasons and conclusion

blocks.text: Use it for a verdict the reader should be able to check reason by reason. Avoid it for a plain fact with one obvious reason; a sentence in a `p` says that faster.

blocks.claim: Reminders should go out three days before the due date.
reasons: Most late returns come back within a week of the due date.
A reminder on the due date itself leaves no time to renew.
blocks.conclusion: So an earlier reminder turns late returns into renewals.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "argument",
  "claim": "Reminders should go out three days before the due date.",
  "reasons": [
    "Most late returns come back within a week of the due date.",
    "A reminder on the due date itself leaves no time to renew."
  ],
  "conclusion": "So an earlier reminder turns late returns into renewals."
}

sections.title: example: one case walked through the process

blocks.text: Use it to follow one concrete item through a process after the general description. Avoid it as the only explanation; without the general rule a reader cannot tell what is typical.

blocks.title: Ana borrows The Hobbit
blocks.setup: Ana brings The Hobbit and her member card to the loan desk.
steps: The librarian scans her card and the book.
The system checks that nobody has reserved it.
It records the loan with a due date three weeks out.
blocks.result: Ana leaves with the book and a receipt, and the loan shows in her account.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "example",
  "title": "Ana borrows The Hobbit",
  "setup": "Ana brings The Hobbit and her member card to the loan desk.",
  "steps": [
    "The librarian scans her card and the book.",
    "The system checks that nobody has reserved it.",
    "It records the loan with a due date three weeks out."
  ],
  "result": "Ana leaves with the book and a receipt, and the loan shows in her account."
}

sections.title: compare: two options side by side

blocks.text: Use it to contrast exactly two options, such as today and a proposal, with a verdict. Avoid it for three or more options or numeric criteria; a `table` compares those.

blocks.title: Paper slips and email reminders
blocks.verdict: Email reminders win, because they arrive when the member can still act.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "compare",
  "title": "Paper slips and email reminders",
  "columns": [
    {"label": "Paper slip", "items": ["Printed at checkout", "Easy to lose"]},
    {
      "label": "Email reminder",
      "items": ["Sent before the due date", "Links straight to renewal"]
    }
  ],
  "verdict": "Email reminders win, because they arrive when the member can still act."
}

sections.title: table: a static table

blocks.text: Use it for a few rows that share columns, such as rules or a scorecard. Avoid it for more than about thirty rows; take `data`, which sorts, searches and pages.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "table",
  "columns": ["Item", "Loan period", "Renewals"],
  "numeric": [2],
  "rows": [
    ["Book", "three weeks", 2],
    ["DVD", "one week", 1],
    ["Magazine", "one week", 0]
  ]
}

sections.title: data: a sortable, searchable table

blocks.text: Use it for a long collection a reader filters, sorts or downloads as CSV. Avoid it for a handful of rows that a static `table` shows at a glance.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "data",
  "id": "loans",
  "label": "Open loans",
  "columns": [
    {"label": "Book", "key": "book"},
    {"label": "Member", "key": "member"},
    {"label": "Due", "key": "due"}
  ],
  "rows": [
    {"book": "The Hobbit", "member": "M-20417", "due": "2026-12-01"},
    {"book": "Atlas of Rivers", "member": "M-20417", "due": "2026-12-01"},
    {"book": "Cooking for One", "member": "M-11873", "due": "2026-11-24"}
  ]
}

sections.title: tree: the entity tree with badge filters

blocks.text: Use it for things that nest, such as steps under an area, when badge filters help a reader narrow them down. Avoid it for a flat list without hierarchy or badges; a `table` is plainer. The tree draws the top-level `entities` and `badges`, so the block itself holds only the filter.

blocks.html: {"type": "tree", "filter": ["who", "state"]}

sections.title: tabs: sibling items side by side

blocks.text: Use it for three or more parallel items of one kind that each need their own blocks. Avoid it for content every reader needs at once, because a closed tab hides it.
A member renews online and returns books at any branch.
A librarian checks books out and clears returns at the desk.
The courier brings each returned book back to its home branch twice a week.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "tabs",
  "id": "roles",
  "label": "Roles",
  "tabs": [
    {
      "label": "Member",
      "summary": "Borrows, renews and returns books.",
      "blocks": [
        {"type": "p", "text": "A member renews online and returns books at any branch."}
      ]
    },
    {
      "label": "Librarian",
      "summary": "Runs the loan desk.",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "p",
          "text": "A librarian checks books out and clears returns at the desk."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "label": "Courier",
      "summary": "Moves returned books between branches.",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "p",
          "text": "The courier brings each returned book back to its home branch twice a week."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

sections.title: bars: simple horizontal bars

blocks.text: Use it for a few counts that need no axis, scripts or CDN. Avoid it for time series or several measures at once; take `vega`.

blocks.html: {"type": "bars", "items": [["Books", 412], ["DVDs", 96], ["Magazines", 38]]}

sections.title: vega: a Vega-Lite chart

blocks.text: Use it for a distribution, a time series or a chart a reader clicks to filter a table. Avoid it when three plain bars say the same; it loads from a CDN and needs JavaScript.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "vega",
  "id": "loans-month",
  "label": "Loans per month",
  "spec": {
    "height": 160,
    "data": {
      "values": [
        {"month": "Aug", "loans": 380},
        {"month": "Sep", "loans": 455},
        {"month": "Oct", "loans": 512}
      ]
    },
    "mark": {"type": "bar", "tooltip": true},
    "encoding": {
      "x": {
        "field": "month",
        "type": "ordinal",
        "sort": null,
        "title": "Month",
        "axis": {"labelAngle": 0}
      },
      "y": {"field": "loans", "type": "quantitative", "title": "Loans"}
    }
  }
}

sections.title: flow: a process or data flow

blocks.text: Use it for how work or data moves between steps, stores and outside actors. Avoid it for a list of steps with no branches or stores; `steps` reads faster.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "flow",
  "id": "lending",
  "label": "From shelf to loan",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "member", "label": "Member", "shape": "external"},
    {"id": "reserve", "label": "Reserve", "sub": "online", "ref": "reserve"},
    {"id": "catalogue", "label": "Catalogue", "shape": "store"},
    {"id": "checkout", "label": "Check out", "sub": "loan desk", "ref": "checkout"},
    {"id": "loans", "label": "Loans", "shape": "store"}
  ],
  "edges": [
    ["member", "reserve", "request"],
    ["reserve", "catalogue", "hold"],
    ["catalogue", "checkout", "book"],
    ["checkout", "loans", "loan"]
  ]
}

sections.title: lineage: how data changes type step by step

blocks.text: Use it to show which function turns one data type into the next. Avoid it for who does what; that is a `flow`.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "lineage",
  "id": "loan-types",
  "label": "Scan to loan record",
  "types": [
    {"id": "scan", "label": "Barcode", "sub": "string"},
    {"id": "copy", "label": "Copy", "sub": "catalogue row", "shape": "store"},
    {"id": "loan", "label": "Loan", "sub": "loans row", "shape": "store"}
  ],
  "steps": [
    {"from": "scan", "to": "copy", "fn": "findCopy()", "note": "looks the barcode up."},
    {
      "from": "copy",
      "to": "loan",
      "fn": "createLoan()",
      "note": "adds member and due date."
    }
  ]
}

sections.title: states: the states of one field

blocks.text: Use it for a status field and the events that move it from state to state. Avoid it for a process across several things; a `flow` shows that.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "states",
  "id": "loan-states",
  "label": "Loan status",
  "field": "loans.status",
  "states": [
    {"id": "open"},
    {"id": "overdue", "color": "red"},
    {"id": "closed", "color": "green"}
  ],
  "transitions": [
    {"from": "[*]", "to": "open", "trigger": "check out"},
    {"from": "open", "to": "overdue", "trigger": "due date passes"},
    {"from": "open", "to": "closed", "trigger": "return"},
    {"from": "overdue", "to": "closed", "trigger": "return"}
  ]
}

sections.title: map: a dependency map

blocks.text: Use it for which systems, services or packages depend on which. Avoid it for an order of steps; a map has no direction of time.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "map",
  "id": "systems",
  "label": "Library systems",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "desk", "label": "Loan desk app"},
    {"id": "web", "label": "Member portal"},
    {"id": "ils", "label": "Library system", "sub": "catalogue and loans"},
    {"id": "mail", "label": "Mail service", "shape": "external"}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"from": "desk", "to": "ils", "label": "loans API"},
    {"from": "web", "to": "ils", "label": "loans API"},
    {"from": "ils", "to": "mail", "label": "reminders"}
  ]
}

sections.title: mermaid: sequence, class, ER and other notations

blocks.text: Use it for a notation the native diagrams lack, such as a sequence of messages or an ER schema. Avoid it for flows and maps, which the native blocks draw without a CDN and with entity links.

blocks.label: Due-date reminder
blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Library system
  participant M as Mail service
  participant R as Member
  S->>M: reminder for loans due in three days
  M->>R: email with renew link
  R->>S: renew

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "mermaid",
  "id": "reminder",
  "label": "Due-date reminder",
  "code": "sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Library system
  participant M as Mail service
  participant R as Member
  S->>M: reminder for loans due in three days
  M->>R: email with renew link
  R->>S: renew"
}

sections.title: board: a moodboard of screens today and proposed

blocks.text: Use it to set today's screens beside a proposal, with marks for what moves, merges or is new. Avoid it for a single screen without a change; a `gallery` shows that.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "board",
  "id": "desk-board",
  "label": "Loan desk today and proposed",
  "canvases": [
    {
      "id": "desk",
      "label": "Loan desk",
      "title": "Loan desk today and proposed",
      "lanes": [
        {
          "tone": "today",
          "cards": [
            {
              "id": "slip",
              "title": "Paper slip",
              "marks": ["remove"],
              "text": "Printed at checkout."
            }
          ],
          "changes": [
            {
              "mark": "new",
              "text": "An email replaces the slip.",
              "from": "slip",
              "to": "email"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "tone": "proposed",
          "cards": [
            {
              "id": "email",
              "title": "Email receipt",
              "marks": ["new"],
              "text": "Sent with the due dates."
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

sections.title: concepts: terms and the interface variants that use them

blocks.text: Use it to settle what a term means and where each variant of a screen shows it, for instance before a rename. Avoid it for data structures; a `lineage` or a `mermaid` ER diagram fits those.

terms.label: Loan
terms.def: A copy a member has borrowed, with a due date.

terms.label: Hold
terms.def: A member's claim on the next free copy.

where.text: Member menu: own entry under My account

blocks.html:

  "kinds": {

    "event": {"label": "Event", "color": "purple"}
  },
  "terms": [
    {
      "id": "loan",

    },
    {

sections.title: mock: dialog sketches compared

blocks.text: Use it to compare two versions of one dialog or form field by field. Avoid it for a whole screen; a screenshot in a `gallery` is more honest.

blocks.label: Renew dialog
notes: Shows the new due date before the member confirms.

blocks.html:
{
  "type": "mock",
  "id": "renew-dialog",
  "label": "Renew dialog",
  "notes": ["Shows the new due date before the member confirms."],
  "panes": [
    {
      "label": "Today",
      "title": "Renew loan",
      "body": [{"label": "Book", "value": "The Hobbit"}],
      "buttons": [{"label": "Cancel"}, {"label": "Renew", "primary": true}]
    },
    {
      "label": "Proposed",
      "title": "Renew loan",
      "body": [
        {"label": "Book", "value": "The Hobbit"},
        {"label": "New due date", "value": "in three weeks", "n": 1}
      ],
      "buttons": [{"label": "Cancel"}, {"label": "Renew", "primary": true}]
    }
  ]
}

sections.title: media: licensed images with credits

blocks.text: Use it for a photo or drawing whose credit and licence the reader must see, as web-research does. Avoid it for screenshots of the product you review; a `gallery` pins notes to them.

items.alt: Reading room with two shelves and a returns trolley
items.caption: Returned books wait on the trolley until a librarian shelves them.

{
  "type": "media",

      "credit": "Drawing for this catalog",
      "license": "CC0 1.0",
      "license_url": "https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"
    }
  ]
}

blocks.text: Use it for screens a reader inspects, with notes pinned where each problem is, as app-audit does. Avoid it for decorative images; `media` carries those with their credits.

sections.title: video: a chaptered explainer video

blocks.text: Use it when the reader asked for a video or animation; `report-video` renders it from the report. Avoid it as the only carrier of an answer, because the page must read without it. The clip here is the bundled `report-video` demo, since a library video would only repeat the same player.

}
